details:
The current radial menu types (Button, Toggle, etc) covers the very basic use cases, but there is a lot of space here for more specialized radial menus. Many of the suggestions under can be solved through animator controllers, but we don't like those for optimization and accessibility reasons. 

~Looping Radial~

A Hue slider tends to go from Red at 0%, through Green (33%) and Blue (66%), and then back to Red (100%).

 In these cases it might be more appropriate to have a "Looping Radial" that goes from 0 to 0.999... and when you hit a full rotation it simply resets, allowing the user to rotate several times both clockwise and counter clockwise. Good for any parameters that loops.

~Sequencer~

Another useful radial menu type would be a button that sequence through several options. In editor you assign a parameter of type Int or Float, then populate a list of values for that parameter.  Activating the button sets the parameter to the next value in the list, looping back around when it reaches the end.  This would be useful for packing several options into one button that you sequence through with each click. Each entry in the list could also have an associated text-field for what the controllers visual name is while that entry is active.

~Preset~

This would be a button that sets several parameters to specific values when activated. In editor it would be a list of parameters and destination values.  Activating it sets all these parameters at once, leaving them there like how a toggle would.

~TwoAxisPoint~

Much like the Two Axis puppet, this would take 2 float/int parameters, one for each axis. But unlike the puppet, it would not reset itself when released. Instead visually the user is presented with a square and a single point inside it. Moving the thumbstick would move the point in that direction at fairly slow speed. Bonus points if the speed (or time-to-reach-edge-from-center factor) is adjustable.
title: More Radial menu types
